builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Structure Over Scale: Rethinking Adaptation for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
summary: The method replaces the default choice of LoRA (or full fine-tuning) for RLVR post-training with structurally constrained adapters, DoRA or QuanTA, which keep updates distributed rather than rank-collapsed. Cost is comparable to LoRA in memory and parameter count (under 0.6% of weights updated), with modest implementation complexity since DoRA is available in standard PEFT libraries, while QuanTA is newer and less supported. Failure modes include overgeneralizing from a single cold-start GRPO protocol, unverified gains on other base models or reward domains, and the untested Model Maturity Hypothesis that the best adapter geometry depends on the base model's pre-training.
rationale: For RLVR post-training of ~8B models on a single 24 GB GPU, structured adapters offer FFT-competitive quality at LoRA-like memory cost, but the evidence is limited to one protocol and a few models, so workload-specific validation is warranted.

claims.statement: The method replaces the default choice of LoRA (or full fine-tuning) for RLVR post-training with structurally constrained adapters, DoRA or QuanTA, which keep updates distributed rather than rank-collapsed. Cost is comparable to LoRA in memory and parameter count (under 0.6% of weights updated), with modest implementation complexity since DoRA is available in standard PEFT libraries, while QuanTA is newer and less supported. Failure modes include overgeneralizing from a single cold-start GRPO protocol, unverified gains on other base models or reward domains, and the untested Model Maturity Hypothesis that the best adapter geometry depends on the base model's pre-training.
DoRA/QuanTA match full fine-tuning while updating under 0.6% of parameters; LoRA collapses from 73.1% accuracy at r=64 to 4.7% at r=128 on DeepMath-Hard, while structured adapters remain stable.
